questions.question: Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.hint: Bats are the only mammals capable of sustained, powered flight. Flying squirrels only glide.

questions.question: What is the largest species of shark?
questions.hint: Despite being the largest fish in the world, whale sharks feed mainly on plankton.

questions.question: Which fictional metal is used to make Wolverine's claws?
questions.hint: Adamantium is the nearly indestructible metal bonded to Wolverine's skeleton.

questions.question: In Finding Nemo, what kind of fish is Nemo?
questions.hint: Nemo is a clownfish living with his father, Marlin, on a coral reef.

questions.question: Which color of recycling bin is commonly used for paper in many countries?
questions.hint: Blue recycling bins are widely used for paper and cardboard, though colors may vary by country.

questions.question: Which organization delivers mail and parcels within a country?
questions.hint: Postal services collect, sort, and deliver letters and packages.

questions.question: Which wall divided East and West Berlin until 1989?
questions.hint: The Berlin Wall became a symbol of the Cold War before it fell in 1989.

questions.question: Which famous ship carried the Pilgrims to North America in 1620?
questions.hint: The Mayflower transported English Pilgrims to present-day Massachusetts.

questions.question: Which country invented the modern sport of basketball?
questions.hint: Basketball was invented in 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts, by James Naismith.

questions.question: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.hint: Most professional golf tournaments are played over 18-hole courses.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent?
questions.hint: Australia is the smallest continent by land area.

questions.question: Which country is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
questions.hint: Finland has around 188,000 lakes, earning it this famous nickname.

questions.question: Which organ is responsible for filtering blood in the human body?
questions.hint: The kidneys remove waste and excess water from the blood to produce urine.

questions.question: Which scientist developed the theory of gravity after observing a falling apple?
questions.hint: According to legend, Newton was inspired by a falling apple to think about gravity.

questions.question: Which country is famous for the dance called Tango?
questions.hint: Tango originated in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in the late 19th century.

questions.question: Which holiday is celebrated on December 25 by many Christians?
questions.hint: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ and is observed worldwide.

questions.question: Which animal is famous for carrying its baby in a pouch?
questions.hint: Female kangaroos carry their young, called joeys, in a pouch until they are developed.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.hint: Russia spans Europe and Asia and covers more land than any other country.

questions.question: Which force keeps planets orbiting around the Sun?
questions.hint: Gravity is the force that attracts objects with mass and keeps planets in orbit.

questions.question: Which famous clock tower is located in London?
questions.hint: Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell inside the famous clock tower at the Palace of Westminster in London.
